title: Direct Detection of Poliovirus and Nanopore Sequencing
author: Erika Bujaki
materials: Add the following reagents to the PCR tube containing the 50 μL purified pool from Step 3.12 :

In the thermocyler, incubate for 5 minutes at 20°C followed by 5 minutes at 65°C Create an End-prep incubation program in the thermocycler: 5 min at 20°C followed by 5 minutes at 65°C, followed by cooling and holding at 10°C.

Prepare reagents and materials for the next steps: Spin down the NEB Quick T4 Ligase and place on ice. Spin down and thaw Ligation Adapter (LA) on ice. Thaw Ligation Buffer (LNB) at room temperature, spin down, mix by pipetting, then place on ice. Thaw Elution Buffer (EB), and Short Fragment Buffer (SFB) at room temperature, mix by vortexing then place on ice. In preparation for the sequencing run, remove the Flush buffer, flush tether (FLT) and BSA from the freezer and thaw at room temperature. Once thawed, place on ice. Take the flow cell out of the fridge, remove it from the black pouch and open the plastic case to allow it reaching room temperature and letting any moisture evaporate.
Prepare the priming mix by adding the following reagents in a clean 1.5mL tube or a 200μL PCR tube: Mix by pipetting, spin down briefly and store on ice until ready to use.
In the MinKNOW software follow the steps below to set up and start your sequencing run.
Amplify using the following cycling conditions:

steps.title: Calculate reactions and controls
steps.instruction: Determine the total number of RT‑PCR reactions needed, including triplicate reactions for each sewage‑concentrate RNA sample, positive and negative RNA extraction controls, and additional PCR positive and negative controls. Use previously stored amplified RNA as the PCR positive control.

steps.title: Make primer working stocks
steps.instruction: Prepare 10 µM primer working solutions by mixing 10 µL of each 100 µM reverse‑primer stock (Y7, AriR/Cre, nOPV‑MM‑R) with 80 µL nuclease‑free water to a final volume of 100 µL (each primer at 10 µM). Freeze any leftover stock. Prepare a 5 µM barcoded primer working stock for the second PCR by adding 10 µL of each 100 µM barcoded Y7 and Q8 primer to 180 µL nuclease‑free water (final 200 µL, each at 5 µM). Freeze leftovers.

steps.title: Prepare RT‑PCR master mix
steps.instruction: Combine the reagents listed in the protocol table (RT‑PCR enzymes, dNTPs, buffer, etc.) in a labelled microcentrifuge tube for the calculated number of reactions plus extra for pipetting loss.

steps.title: Aliquot master mix
steps.instruction: Briefly vortex and centrifuge the RT‑PCR master mix, then dispense 16 µL into each PCR tube.

steps.title: Reverse transcription incubation
steps.instruction: Flick each tube gently to mix, briefly centrifuge, then incubate at 50 °C for 30 min and cool to 10 °C at the end of the program. Only reverse primers are present at this stage.

steps.title: Add forward primer after RT
steps.instruction: Briefly centrifuge the tubes after the RT step and add 1 µL of the 10 µM forward‑primer working stock to each tube using a fresh pipette tip for each addition.

steps.title: First‑round PCR amplification
steps.instruction: Run the RT‑PCR tubes in a thermocycler using the cycling conditions supplied in the protocol (amplicon ≈2 kb).

steps.title: Prepare second‑PCR mastermix
steps.instruction: Combine the second‑PCR reagents (polymerase, buffer, dNTPs, etc.) in a labelled tube for the required number of reactions plus extra for loss.

steps.title: Aliquot second‑PCR mix and primers
steps.instruction: Aliquot 21 µL of the second‑PCR mastermix into each well of a 96‑well plate, then add 2 µL of the appropriate 5 µM barcoded primer mix (unique barcode per sample).

steps.title: Add first‑round product
steps.instruction: Add 2 µL of the first‑round PCR product from the RT‑PCR tubes to each corresponding well. For the PCR negative control, add nuclease‑free water instead of product.

steps.title: Add RNA template
steps.instruction: Add 8 µL of sample RNA, control RNA, or nuclease‑free water (for the PCR negative control) to each well.

steps.title: Pool barcoded amplicons
steps.instruction: Pool an equal volume (e.g., 2 µL) of each barcoded amplicon into a single tube; change tips between samples to avoid cross‑contamination.

steps.title: Add AMPure beads to pool
steps.instruction: Add room‑temperature AMPure beads equal in volume to the pooled amplicons (e.g., 100 µL beads for a 100 µL pool).

steps.title: Bind DNA to beads
steps.instruction: Mix the pool and beads by gently flicking, incubate at room temperature for 5 min, then flick again to keep the mixture homogeneous.

steps.title: Check PCR products on gel
steps.instruction: Run all first‑ and second‑round PCR controls on agarose gel electrophoresis to confirm successful amplification of the positive control and absence of contamination in negative controls.

steps.title: Magnetic bead cleanup – first wash
steps.instruction: Place the tube on a magnetic rack until the solution clears, pipette off the supernatant, then add 200 µL of 80 % ethanol, wait 30 s, remove supernatant. Repeat the ethanol wash once more.

steps.title: Dry and elute DNA
steps.instruction: Spin the tube for ~3 s, keep on magnet, remove residual ethanol, air‑dry the bead pellet for ~30 s (avoid over‑drying), then add 51 µL nuclease‑free water, flick to resuspend, incubate at room temperature for 2 min.

steps.title: Collect eluate
steps.instruction: Remove 50 µL of the eluate and transfer to a clean, labelled 0.2 mL PCR tube.

steps.title: End‑preparation of pooled amplicons
steps.instruction: Pool 2 µL of each barcoded amplicon (as before), flick to mix, spin briefly, then add 60 µL of room‑temperature AMPure beads (vortexed to resuspend). Transfer 60 µL of the end‑prep reaction (from the kit) into the same tube, mix gently, and incubate at room temperature for 5 min, flicking once after 2 min.

steps.title: Bead cleanup after end‑prep – first wash
steps.instruction: Spin briefly, place on magnet, remove supernatant, add 200 µL 80 % ethanol, wait 30 s, remove supernatant. Repeat the ethanol wash once.

steps.title: Dry and elute end‑prep DNA
steps.instruction: Spin 3 s, keep on magnet, remove residual ethanol, air‑dry pellet for ~30 s, then add 61 µL nuclease‑free water, flick to resuspend, incubate at room temperature for 2 min.

steps.title: Collect end‑prep eluate
steps.instruction: Spin briefly, place on magnet, remove 60 µL of eluate and transfer to a clean 1.5 mL LoBind tube. Store at 4 °C (up to 1 week) or proceed immediately.

steps.title: Adapter ligation reaction
steps.instruction: Prepare the adapter ligation mix by adding the kit reagents (sequencing adapters, ligase, buffer, etc.) to the tube containing the end‑prep DNA, flick to mix, and incubate at room temperature for 10 min.

steps.title: Library bead cleanup with SFB
steps.instruction: Vortex AMPure beads, add 40 µL of the resuspended beads to the ligation reaction, flick to mix, incubate at room temperature for 5 min (flick after 2 min).

steps.title: Run flow‑cell check
steps.instruction: In MinKNOW, start a flow‑cell check (or a dummy 0.2‑h run if pore count is low) to assess available pores before loading the library.

steps.title: Magnetic cleanup after ligation – SFB washes
steps.instruction: Spin briefly, place on magnet, discard supernatant, add 250 µL Short Fragment Buffer (SFB), resuspend beads by flicking, spin 3 s, place on magnet, discard supernatant. Repeat the SFB wash once more, then spin, place on magnet, remove residual SFB, and air‑dry the pellet for 1 min.

steps.title: Elute final library
steps.instruction: Add 15 µL Elution Buffer (EB) to the dried beads, flick gently, incubate at room temperature for 10 min (flick a few times during incubation), spin 3 s, place on magnet, and remove 12 µL of eluate into a clean 1.5 mL tube. Store at 4 °C (short‑term) or proceed to sequencing.

steps.title: Prepare sequencing reagents
steps.instruction: Thaw Sequencing Buffer (SB), Library Beads (LIB), Flow Cell Tether (FCT), BSA, and Flow Cell Flush (FCF) at room temperature, then keep on ice. Vortex SB, FCF, and FCT, spin down, and return to ice. Spin LIB and keep on ice.

steps.title: Prime flow cell
steps.instruction: Remove the flow cell from the device, place it back in its case, open the priming‑port cover clockwise, inspect for bubbles, and remove any bubbles with a P1000 pipette. Load 800 µL of priming mix (SB + FCF + FCT) via the priming port, leaving a small volume in the tip to avoid air, then incubate 5 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare library mix for loading
steps.instruction: In a clean tube, combine the Sequencing Buffer (SB) and Library Beads (LIB) with the adapter‑ligated, cleaned library from the previous step. Mix gently by pipetting.

steps.title: Complete flow‑cell priming
steps.instruction: Open the SpotOn port cover, slowly load 200 µL of the prepared library mix through the SpotOn port (leaving a small volume in the tip to prevent bubbles), then close the SpotOn cover and the priming port.

steps.title: Load library onto flow cell
steps.instruction: Load the remaining library mix dropwise via the SpotOn port, allowing each drop to flow into the flow cell before adding the next.

steps.title: Start sequencing run
steps.instruction: In MinKNOW, click Start, create a unique run name (date + experiment), select kit SQK‑LSK114, enable barcoding (EXP‑PBC096) with barcode at both ends, set run time to 6–12 h (depending on sample number and pore count), choose High‑Accuracy basecalling, then start the run.

steps.title: Post‑run flow‑cell wash
steps.instruction: Thaw Wash Diluent (WMX) at room temperature, vortex briefly, spin down, and keep on ice. Prepare the wash solution in a clean 1.5 mL tube. Open the priming port, remove any bubbles, add 200 µL of wash solution, incubate 5 min at room temperature, then add the remaining 200 µL, incubate 1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Remove waste and label flow cell
steps.instruction: After incubation, remove all waste from the waste channel while keeping the priming port closed. Optionally label the flow‑cell packaging with run date, sample details, run time, and barcodes used.

steps.title: Store flow cell for future use
steps.instruction: If the flow cell will be stored, thaw the Storage Buffer (from the Wash Kit) at room temperature, vortex briefly, then slowly add 500 µL through the priming port. Close the priming port, remove any remaining waste, place the flow cell back in its plastic box and store at 4 °C.
